name: security-elasticsearch-document-security-review
artifacts: Roles, index patterns/aliases, document/field restrictions, query identity and alternative read APIs.
trace: Trace index/alias resolution and the actual security filter applied to the requested operation, including owned search/export paths.
experiment: Use synthetic documents for two owned tenants and compare an entitled query with a known foreign-document request through a relevant supported API.
disproof: An index name or intentionally shared aggregate is not a document leak; admin query success does not establish a user bypass.
repair: Bind effective index/document policy across intended APIs and retest authorized searches and foreign markers.
branch_decisions: Determine how multiple roles combine and whether document/field restrictions apply to the actual API and license/configuration. An alias is not inherently an authorization boundary. Compare search, direct document and alternate permitted paths with owned markers; an aggregation count or a metadata field can be a distinct limited disclosure rather than full document access.
operational_method: Compute the effective same-index role combination: DLS grants combine by OR, and a role granting that index without DLS can remove the document restriction; field permissions combine by union. These read restrictions are not a general write policy. Retain every applicable role and index/alias match, then compare two synthetic documents/fields under the merged roles. A correct filtered search under one isolated role does not establish the actual user restriction.
